correctness.rationale: The exact prior classification and all analytic steps have been checked. Elementary pairwise prime divisibility moments yield O(X log log X) variance, Chebyshev removes o(X/log log log X) exceptions, and strict threshold implications handle both squarefree and repeated least primes. Uniform short inclusion–exclusion and Mertens product give constant e^{-gamma}; t below, equal to, and above 1 are treated separately. Verification script checks exact finite identities only.

evidence: Jia–Li Theorem 2 settles the broader pointwise structural membership criterion but not the population distribution; de la Bretèche–Ford–Vandehey maximize the size of disjoint progression families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Pointwise membership is logically weaker than a global counting asymptotic and Pareto conditional limit unless analytic density and concentration inputs are added. The unrelated maximization theorem cannot dominate this law.

value.rationale: Determines a natural global counting invariant and complete fixed-threshold distribution for the full class of integers carrying a divisor-moduli residue assignment. The ultraslow triple-logarithmic zero-density scale and nondegenerate Pareto law distinguish the typical least-prime-factor geometry not determined by mere membership or any arbitrary finite cutoff; no large downstream theorem is asserted.
